reden: Yes. The audit explicitly flags TimelockTokenPool.sol withdraw(address, bytes) for using a replayable signature (hashing only the '_to' string without nonce/deadline/contract/chain binding or used-sig tracking). It notes anyone can call withdraw(_to, sig) repeatedly (even across pool instances), withdrawing all currently unlocked tokens each time. This matches the described vulnerability’s root cause, function, and attack path; the same fix (add nonce/deadline/contract/chain binding and/or mark signatures as used) would resolve both.
